title: Cervical cancer screening program: Review of literature
abstract: Objectives: The objective of the study is to evaluate the results of cervical cancer screening and human papillomavirus (HPV) testing, with a review of the HPV vaccination program and to identify cytological patterns based on the 2014 Bethesda System and HPV status in Bahraini women across different age groups from 2020 to 2023. Materials and Methods: This retrospective study analyzed the results of all cervical cytology smears and HPV status in Bahrain from 2020 to 2023 using the 2014 Bethesda System for Reporting Cervical Cytology. Results: Of the 24,159 cervical papanicolaou (PAP) smears studied, 22,218 (92%) were negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM), and 1941 (8%) were abnormal; high-risk HPV (hrHPV) test was performed on 789 cases. Among these, 8.7% were NILM, 52.1% were atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance or high-grade lesions cannot be excluded (ASCUS/ASCH), and 3.2% were malignant. Abnormal findings were higher in the 40–49 years age group. HPV 16 was detected in 9.8% of cases, HPV 18–45 in 3.8% of cases, and other high-risk HPV (hrHPV) in 20.8% of cases, while 79.2% tested negative. HPV 16, 18–45, and other hrHPV types were prevalent in the 30–49-year age group. Conclusion: The highest prevalence of abnormal findings was in the ASCUS/ASCH category, particularly in younger women, suggesting the need for careful monitoring to prevent progression to higher-grade lesions. The findings align with global patterns, where hrHPV peaks in younger women and declines with age, indicating the importance of age-specific screening. The presence of HPV 16 and other high-risk types in women aged 30–49 highlights the importance of HPV vaccination and regular screening.

Results: Of the 24,159 cervical papanicolaou (PAP) smears studied, 22,218 (92%) were negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM), and 1941 (8%) were abnormal; high-risk HPV (hrHPV) test was performed on 789 cases. Among these, 8.7% were NILM, 52.1% were atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance or high-grade lesions cannot be excluded (ASCUS/ASCH), and 3.2% were malignant. Abnormal findings were higher in the 40–49 years age group. HPV 16 was detected in 9.8% of cases, HPV 18–45 in 3.8% of cases, and other high-risk HPV (hrHPV) in 20.8% of cases, while 79.2% tested negative. HPV 16, 18–45, and other hrHPV types were prevalent in the 30–49-year age group. Conclusion: The highest prevalence of abnormal findings was in the ASCUS/ASCH category, particularly in younger women, suggesting the need for careful monitoring to prevent progression to higher-grade lesions. The findings align with global patterns, where hrHPV peaks in younger women and declines with age, indicating the importance of age-specific screening. The presence of HPV 16 and other high-risk types in women aged 30–49 highlights the importance of HPV vaccination and regular screening.

title: Menstrual, reproductive, and contraceptive factors associated with cervical cancer in women aged ≤35 years: an individually matched case–control study
abstract: Objective This study aims to investigate the associations of menstrual, reproductive, and contraceptive characteristics with early-onset cervical cancer among women aged ≤35 years. Methods A hospital-based, individually matched case–control study was conducted at West China Second University Hospital from January 2022 to December 2024. A total of 300 women aged ≤35 years and with histologically confirmed cervical cancer were individually matched 1:1 to 300 screening controls within 0.5 years of age and 7 days of recruitment. Menstrual, reproductive, and contraceptive histories accrued up to 90 days before the index data were collected through standardized interviews and medical record reviews. Separate exposure-specific conditional logistic regression models stratified by matched pair were adjusted for prespecified sociodemographic, behavioral, screening-related, infection-related, and current high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) covariates. The model samples ranged from 189 to 277 matched pairs. Exploratory subgroup analyses assessed effect modification. Results In the fully adjusted model, menstrual period duration was associated with early-onset cervical cancer, with evidence of nonlinearity ( P for nonlinearity <0.001). Each 1-year increase in age at first pregnancy was associated with lower odds (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.717; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.561–0.917). Higher odds were associated with greater gravidity (aOR per pregnancy, 2.959; 95% CI, 1.734–5.050), greater parity (aOR per birth, 3.667; 95% CI, 1.886–7.133), and more induced abortions (aOR per event, 2.672; 95% CI, 1.236–5.773). Longer total breastfeeding duration was inversely associated (aOR per 12 months, 0.189; 95% CI, 0.064–0.560), whereas longer cumulative combined oral contraceptive use was positively associated (aOR per 12 months, 1.335; 95% CI, 1.062–1.678). Age at menarche, menstrual cycle irregularity, ever breastfeeding, categorical combined oral contraceptive status, and other contraceptive methods were not statistically significant after full adjustment. No interaction remained statistically significant after false discovery rate correction. Conclusions Selected menstrual, reproductive, and contraceptive characteristics were associated with early-onset cervical cancer after adjustment for measured confounders and current hrHPV status.

title: Editorial: Prevention and early detection of oral cancers – volume II
abstract: Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma (OSCC) remains the most common type of oral cancer, primarily originating from the epithelial lining of the oral cavity, and continues to represent a significant global health concern with persistently high mortality despite the accessibility of the oral cavity to clinical examination [1]. The occurrence of diagnostic delay, caused by clinical overlaps with non-cancerous diseases and drug-related adverse events, plays a crucial part in determining prognosis and outcomes of the disease [2]. In this Research Topic entitled Prevention and Early Detection of Oral Cancers-Volume II, five different contributions will cover different topics within the area, such as diagnostic overlap in OSCC and MRONJ in patients treated with bone-modifying agents, HPV-associated lesions, imaging technology in oral oncology, epidemiology of risk factors, and educational efforts in early oral cancer detection. Five different articles will discuss different, yet related, aspects of the topic, namely diagnostic overlap in OSCC and MRONJ in patients receiving bone-modifying drugs, diagnosis and management of HPV-related oral lesions, optical imaging in oral oncology and OPMDs, epidemiology of smoking as a risk factor for developing oral and pharyngeal cancer, and an educational intervention in the diagnosis of oral cancers.A central diagnostic challenge addressed in this volume concerns the differentiation of OSCC from conditions that closely mimic its presentation. According to Mauceri et al., a group of eleven patients treated with bone modifying agent or anti-angiogenic therapies had OSCC showing similar clinical and radiological appearances as MRONJ. These eleven out of a total of 711 patients originally suspected of suffering from MRONJ were eventually found to have OSCC based on results obtained through biopsy, with the mandible being the most common area of involvement. Some of the overlapping characteristics observed in the cases include bone exposure, mucosal defect, soft tissue swelling, and cortical erosion. This suggests that while biopsy may not be necessary for the diagnosis of MRONJ, biopsy should be considered for patients taking bone-modifying agents, even at a lower dose for osteoporosis treatment, when there is suspicion of malignancy (Mauceri et al.).Another parallel problem in diagnosis is discussed by Anaya-Saavedra et al., presenting their brief discussion about HPV-OLs. In this review, the four types of HPV-OL, such as squamous papilloma, verruca vulgaris, condyloma acuminatum, and multifocal epithelial hyperplasia, are presented along with their distinct but commonly overlapping characteristics, making their classification difficult to identify. Two common myths about HPV-OLs are debunked in this paper. The first myth is about sexual transmission because of compelling proof that HPV-OLs can be transmitted horizontally, by autoinoculation, perinatally, or via fomites. Meanwhile, the second myth is about their malignant potential because these lesions are generally caused by low-risk HPV genotypes that are in the form of an episome and not chromosomal instability like that seen in dysplastic transformation. The paper concludes that conservative surgery remains the only treatment available, while topical medications used for dermatologic and anogenital treatments may cause harmful effects on the oral mucosa. source_records.abstract: Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma (OSCC) remains the most common type of oral cancer, primarily originating from the epithelial lining of the oral cavity, and continues to represent a significant global health concern with persistently high mortality despite the accessibility of the oral cavity to clinical examination [1]. The occurrence of diagnostic delay, caused by clinical overlaps with non-cancerous diseases and drug-related adverse events, plays a crucial part in determining prognosis and outcomes of the disease [2]. In this Research Topic entitled Prevention and Early Detection of Oral Cancers-Volume II, five different contributions will cover different topics within the area, such as diagnostic overlap in OSCC and MRONJ in patients treated with bone-modifying agents, HPV-associated lesions, imaging technology in oral oncology, epidemiology of risk factors, and educational efforts in early oral cancer detection. Five different articles will discuss different, yet related, aspects of the topic, namely diagnostic overlap in OSCC and MRONJ in patients receiving bone-modifying drugs, diagnosis and management of HPV-related oral lesions, optical imaging in oral oncology and OPMDs, epidemiology of smoking as a risk factor for developing oral and pharyngeal cancer, and an educational intervention in the diagnosis of oral cancers.A central diagnostic challenge addressed in this volume concerns the differentiation of OSCC from conditions that closely mimic its presentation. title: TGF-β-induced epithelial to mesenchymal transition drives proteoglycan binding specificity of HPV-based drug conjugates for cancer cells
abstract: Background Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) utilize specifically modified proteoglycans (PGs) within the basement membrane as attachment factors prior to cell entry and infection. Similarly modified PGs are also found on cancer cells, which enables HPV with tumor-selective binding properties and highlights the potential development of HPV capsid-based anti-cancer therapies. In this study, we sought to investigate cancer-specific gene signatures and genetic factors that give rise to selective binding by HPV capsids. Methods Using belzupacap sarotalocan (bel-sar; AU-011), an HPV virus-like drug conjugate (HPV-VDC) currently in clinical trials, we performed a cell binding screen using 115 cancer cell lines from which we performed gene expressions analysis. We developed drug resistant lines to investigate the developmental factors involved in tumor targeting. Results We identified a strong association between drug binding and pathways involved in TGF-β-induced epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT). Furthermore, dose escalation treatments leading to selection of bel-sar resistant HeLa cells resulted in a marked reduction in TGF-β signaling and reversal of EMT, which was associated with a reduction in the synthesis and expression of heparan- and chondroitin sulfate proteoglycans. Conclusion Overall, these data suggest that bel-sar binding is strongly dependent on the differential expression and modification of PGs that occurs during the EMT process. As many cancers undergo EMT during progression and invasion, these data provide mechanistic insights underlying the tumor-selective binding ability of HPV-VDCs.

title: Distinct Molecular Landscape and Clinical Subtype of HPV-Positive Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma
abstract: Background: This study aimed to investigate the prevalence of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in Chinese patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and its association with driver gene mutations (EGFR, KRAS, PIK3CA, PTEN), clinicopathological features, and prognosis. Methods: A retrospective cohort of 120 Chinese ESCC patients was analyzed. HPV infection status and typing were determined by polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based reverse hybridization in tumor tissues; EGFR, KRAS, PIK3CA, and PTEN mutations were assessed by Sanger sequencing. Associations with clinicopathological variables and survival were evaluated. Results: The HPV infection rate was 44.2%, with 37.5% single-type and 6.7% mixed infections, predominantly high-risk types. No EGFR or KRAS mutations were detected, whereas PTEN and PIK3CA mutations were found in 16.7% and 6.7% of patients, respectively, and were mutually exclusive. HPV-negative tumors more frequently showed lymphovascular invasion (p = 0.03) and PTEN mutations (p = 0.017). HPV positivity was associated with better recurrence-free survival and overall survival. Conclusions: HPV infection is prevalent in Chinese ESCC and may delineate a distinct molecular profile; HPV-negative ESCC was more frequently associated with aggressive clinicopathological features, including lymphovascular invasion and PTEN mutations. These findings support subtype-stratified prevention and treatment strategies for ESCC.

title: Context-specific strategies for enhancing HPV vaccination: key informant perspectives from selected U.S. jurisdictions in the post-COVID-19 era
abstract: Introduction Despite the availability of a safe and effective Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine, uptake remains inconsistent across the United States (U.S.), with marked differences in vaccination coverage across states. This descriptive exploratory study examined key informant perspectives on HPV vaccination promotion across policy-engaged jurisdictions in the U.S. in the post-COVID-19 era. Methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with nine key informants across six U.S. Classification of the interviews was based on those with existing HPV vaccine school-entry requirements or those jurisdictions with recent school-entry policy considerations. Using inductive thematic analysis, we synthesized key informant perspectives and organized themes using analytical dimensions informed by the socio-ecological model. Results Findings highlight the importance of provider education, school-entry requirements, cancer prevention messaging, trusted messengers, culturally tailored outreach, and cross-sector partnerships as important components of HPV vaccine promotion. Barriers such as vaccine misinformation and increased hesitancy following the COVID-19 pandemic were also discussed. Discussion These insights can inform targeted, context-specific strategies to improve HPV vaccination rates and reduce cancer disparities.

This descriptive exploratory study examined key informant perspectives on HPV vaccination promotion across policy-engaged jurisdictions in the U.S. in the post-COVID-19 era. Methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with nine key informants across six U.S. Classification of the interviews was based on those with existing HPV vaccine school-entry requirements or those jurisdictions with recent school-entry policy considerations. Using inductive thematic analysis, we synthesized key informant perspectives and organized themes using analytical dimensions informed by the socio-ecological model. Results Findings highlight the importance of provider education, school-entry requirements, cancer prevention messaging, trusted messengers, culturally tailored outreach, and cross-sector partnerships as important components of HPV vaccine promotion. Barriers such as vaccine misinformation and increased hesitancy following the COVID-19 pandemic were also discussed. Discussion These insights can inform targeted, context-specific strategies to improve HPV vaccination rates and reduce cancer disparities.

title: Immune remodeling in HPV-associated cervical disease
abstract: Introduction Persistent high-risk HPV infection is the principal cause of cervical dysplasia, but variation in disease phenotype may also be associated with differences in the local immune and microbial environment. Methods We characterized the cervicovaginal immune microenvironment in relation to HPV status, vaginal community state type (CST), and cytological grade. Results HPV-positive samples showed reduced IL-4 and IL-17E/IL-25, while IFN-α2 and IL-3 varied across community state types in a non-monotonic, CST-specific manner: IFN-α2 was relatively elevated in the Lactobacillus gasseri -dominant CST II, and IL-3 was specifically reduced in the Lactobacillus jensenii -dominant CST V. Cytological category was associated with non-monotonic, marker-specific immune variation, with LSIL showing lower IL-4, IFN-γ, IL-17F, PDGF-AB/BB, IL-17E/IL-25, and PDGF-AA levels relative to NILM, while ASC-H showed a distinct rather than uniformly progressive immune profile. CLR-based multi-kingdom analyses identified a restricted set of taxon–cytokine associations after correction of the relative-abundance scale, prespecified prevalence and abundance filtering, and multiple-testing correction. Significant bacterial associations were confined to the genus level, whereas viral associations were observed at the family, genus, and species levels and fungal associations at the family level. Phocaeicola–IL-10 and Rountreeviridae–MIP-1β were the only associations that additionally remained significant after global BH-FDR correction across all taxon–immune-marker tests. Viral and fungal findings were interpreted as exploratory because of substantially lower non-bacterial sequencing depth. Discussion These microbial associations provide additional context for the observed immune-marker differences. These findings support further investigation of multi-kingdom host–microbiome immune relationships in HPV-associated cervical abnormalities.

title: Raman-spectroscopy: diagnostic value, risk stratification and future perspectives in HPV-associated cervical lesions: a review
abstract: Cervical cancer continues to rank among the leading causes of cancer morbidity and mortality in women worldwide, underscoring the urgent need for innovative non-invasive, objective, and highly sensitive diagnostic methodologies, particularly for the early identification of lesions associated with the human papillomavirus (HPV). The advancement of such diagnostic techniques aligns with the World Health Organization's global strategy to eradicate cervical cancer as a public health concern. This review consolidates current findings regarding the application of Raman spectroscopy, including its surface-enhanced modality, in the diagnosis and risk stratification of cervical pathology. The analysis revealed that spectral examination of various biological samples – such as cytological preparations of the cervix, blood serum, and cervicovaginal fluid – facilitates the differentiation of benign, precancerous, and malignant conditions based on biochemical alterations in the composition of proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, glycogen, and other metabolites. Noteworthy emphasis is placed on the potential of identifying molecular abnormalities in morphologically unchanged cells, as well as the use of cervicovaginal fluid as a local substrate for liquid biopsy. This development presents promising opportunities for minimally invasive screening and monitoring. The integration of machine learning algorithms and multivariate statistical analysis significantly enhances the diagnostic accuracy of this methodology. However, it is important to note that limited sample sizes and protocol heterogeneity constrain existing studies. Consequently, Raman spectroscopy shows considerable promise for the early diagnosis and risk stratification of human papillomavirus-related cervical lesions. Nevertheless, its clinical implementation requires standardization of methodology, validation of diagnostic models in large independent cohorts, and further investigation into the predictive value of spectral markers.

title: Leveraging exosomes and lipid nanoparticles based nanomedicine for cervical cancer therapeutics
abstract: Cervical cancer (CC) remains a significant global health burden, ranking as the fourth most common cancer among women worldwide. Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) is the primary etiological factor, although tumor progression is also influenced by genetic alterations, immune dysregulation, and changes within the tumor microenvironment. Current therapeutic approaches, including surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and targeted treatment, often lack sufficient tumor specificity, resulting in damage to healthy tissues, treatment-related toxicity, and limited therapeutic efficacy. Nanomedicine has emerged as a promising strategy to address these limitations. Exosomes and lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are biocompatible and, in many cases, biodegradable delivery systems capable of transporting anticancer drugs, nucleic acids, and combination therapies. Their ability to enhance tumor accumulation, protect therapeutic cargo, and reduce systemic exposure may improve treatment outcomes. Furthermore, surface modification with lipid-like moieties, antibodies, peptides, or other targeting ligands can promote selective uptake by CC cells and stromal components of the tumor microenvironment. These nanocarriers may also help overcome drug resistance and facilitate synergistic therapeutic combinations. This review summarizes the pathophysiology of CC and examines recent advances in exosome- and LNP-based therapeutic platforms, including clinically approved nanoparticle formulations and emerging translational studies. We discuss their advantages, limitations, safety considerations, and future prospects for precision treatment, with the goal of improving efficacy, reducing adverse effects, and enhancing patient survival and quality of life.

title: HPV knowledge, awareness, and vaccine beliefs among women attending gynecological care in Türkiye: implications for cervical cancer prevention
abstract: Abstract Background Despite the availability of effective HPV vaccines, vaccination rates remain low in many countries, including Türkiye. Cervical cancer prevention continues to rely largely on opportunistic screening. Although HPV knowledge, awareness, and vaccine beliefs are recognized as important determinants of vaccination behavior, how these factors interact among women attending gynecological care has not been fully elucidated. Methods This cross-sectional study included 300 women aged 18–49 years attending the obstetrics and gynecology outpatient clinic of a university hospital in the Marmara region of Türkiye for gynecological examination. Data were collected using a sociodemographic questionnaire, the HPV Knowledge Scale (HPV-KS), the Human Papilloma Virus Awareness and Concern Scale (HPV-ACS), and the Carolina HPV Vaccination Attitudes and Beliefs Scale (CHPV-VABS). Group comparisons, correlation analyses, and multivariate analysis of variance were performed to examine associations between participant characteristics and HPV knowledge, awareness and concern, and vaccine beliefs. Results Participants showed limited HPV knowledge (11.01 ± 8.77 out of 33), moderate HPV-related awareness and concern (43.57 ± 9.95), and moderate HPV vaccine attitudes and beliefs (37.18 ± 7.42). HPV vaccination uptake was low, with only 12.3% of participants reporting prior vaccination. Higher educational attainment was associated with greater HPV knowledge scores ( p p p =.044, η2 p = .05). Correlation analyses showed strong positive associations between HPV knowledge and HPV-related awareness and concern ( r = .60, 95% CI [0.52, 0.67], p r = .61, 95% CI [0.53, 0.68], p r = − .16, 95% CI [− 0.27, − 0.05], p = .005). Conclusion Women attending gynecological examinations demonstrated limited HPV knowledge and very low HPV vaccination uptake despite moderate levels of HPV-related awareness and concern. These findings suggest that awareness alone may be insufficient to promote vaccination and highlight the importance of improving HPV knowledge through targeted educational interventions. As higher educational attainment was associated with greater HPV knowledge, integrating structured counseling and evidence-based communication into routine gynecological care may help address knowledge gaps and strengthen cervical cancer prevention efforts in Türkiye.

title: Single-cell analysis identifies TOP2α as a critical regulator of G2/M entry and differentiation-dependent productive HPV replication
abstract: High-risk human papillomaviruses (HPVs) are the etiological agents of over 5% of cancers worldwide including those of the cervix and oropharynx. HPVs infect stratified epithelia and establish latent infections in basal cells but restrict productive replication or amplification to differentiated suprabasal cells. Despite the presence of viral genomes in most differentiated cells, only a subset of cells amplifies genomes as well as express late genes and these correspond to those that have re-entered G2/M, but the factors regulating this selectivity are unknown. To determine the signals that control the productive viral life cycle, single cell RNA seq was performed on cells that stably maintain high-risk HPV genomes following differentiation. Ten populations of undifferentiated and differentiating keratinocytes were identified, however, only one differentiated population had entered G2/M, expressed late genes and amplified viral genomes. One of the highly expressed replication factors in this population was the type II topoisomerase TOP2α while no other topoisomerases were similarly induced. TOP2α was found to bind to viral genomes, and acute depletion in differentiating cells blocked entry into G2/M, impaired genome amplification and abrogated late gene expression. Amplification also requires activation of DNA repair pathways through the induction of high levels of DNA breaks, and TOP2α accounted for more than half of the breaks present in differentiating cells. Increases in levels of TOP2α in differentiating cells were driven by the E7 oncoprotein acting through the transcription factor FOXM1, which also controls expression of G2/M factors suggesting an auto-regulatory loop. These studies identify TOP2α as a critical regulator of HPV genome amplification upon differentiation.

title: Long-term Antiretroviral Therapy and Anogenital Cancer Risk.
abstract: BACKGROUND: People with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) (PWH) experience substantially increased risk of anogenital cancer. Whether long-term antiretroviral therapy (ART) reduces anogenital cancer risk is unknown. METHODS: A target trial emulation using a case-cohort design among Botswana adults aged 30-65, sampled via a probability-based household survey across 30 communities. Cases of cervical, vulvar, anal, and penile cancer were prospectively ascertained at the country's principal treatment centers. We estimated the marginal relative risk (RR) of incident anogenital cancer by ART duration, compared with adults without HIV, using g-computation from weighted models that accounted for shared determinants of human papillomavirus, and HIV infection, access to cancer care, and ART duration. RESULTS: 14 312 participants were enrolled (42% PWH), including 1045 (79% PWH) with incident anogenital cancer-792 cervical, 106 vulvar, 80 anal, and 67 penile cancers. Compared with people without HIV, the marginal RR (95% CI) of anogenital cancer increased with longer durations of ART (P = .001) (no ART: 4.6; 4.3-5.0; <5 years: 4.0; 3.7-4.3; 5-9 years: 4.6; 4.2-5.0; ≥10 years: 7.4; 6.8-8.1). Individuals receiving ART for ≥10 years had the highest RR for each cancer evaluated: cervix, 4.4 (4.0 to 4.8); vulva, 36 (22-57); anus, 15 (11-20); and penis, 102 (42-250). Prior advanced HIV disease was associated with increased risk but this effect diminished on ART and contributed relatively little to overall risk. CONCLUSIONS: Long-term utilization of ART was not associated with a reduction in anogenital cancer risk. Improved prevention strategies are needed for PWH.

title: Risk factors for HR-HPV persistence and residual or recurrent high-grade squamous intraepithelial neoplasia after LEEP
abstract: Background To investigate factors associated with persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection and residual or recurrent disease in patients with high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) following loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP). Methods A total of 903 patients with pathologically confirmed HSIL who underwent LEEP between January 2021 and May 2024 were retrospectively enrolled. HR-HPV genotyping and cervical cytology were performed before and after surgery, and residual or recurrent HSIL was assessed by colposcopy during follow-up. Generalized estimating equation (GEE) logistic regression accounted for within-patient clustering of genotype-specific HPV observations. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with HR-HPV persistence, and Firth's penalized logistic regression evaluated factors associated with residual or recurrent HSIL. Results Persistent HR-HPV infection rates were 23.3%, 19.0%, and 17.5% at 6, 12, and 18 months after LEEP, respectively. GEE analysis showed significant differences in type-specific persistence among the α 5/6, α 7, and α 9 species ( P = 0.024), with higher persistence in α 5/6 than α 7 (27.1% vs. 14.0%; OR = 2.30, 95% CI, 1.09–4.85; adjusted P = 0.024), but no significant differences between α 5/6 and α 9 or between α 7 and α 9. Multiple HR-HPV infections (OR = 2.76, 95% CI, 1.96–3.89; P < 0.001) and menopausal status (OR = 2.06, 95% CI, 1.18–3.66; P = 0.011), and positive endocervical margins (OR = 2.54, 95% CI, 1.48–4.32; P = 0.007) were associated with HR-HPV persistence. During follow-up, 32 patients (3.5%) developed residual or recurrent HSIL (21 residual, 11 recurrent). Firth's penalized regression identified persistent type-specific HR-HPV infection (OR = 21.88, 95% CI, 8.25–72.76; P < 0.001), number of involved cervical quadrants ( P = 0.025), endocervical involvement ( P = 0.006), and surgical margin status ( P < 0.001) as independently associated with residual or recurrent HSIL. Conclusions α 5/6 species showed a higher type-specific HR-HPV persistence than α 7 but not α 9 following LEEP. Multiple HR-HPV infections, menopausal status, and positive endocervical margins were associated with HR-HPV persistence. Persistent type-specific HR-HPV infection, multiple involved cervical quadrants, endocervical involvement, and positive surgical margins were independent predictors of residual or recurrent HSIL. Multicenter studies are warranted to validate integrating margin status with HPV genotyping for postoperative risk stratification.

Methods A total of 903 patients with pathologically confirmed HSIL who underwent LEEP between January 2021 and May 2024 were retrospectively enrolled. HR-HPV genotyping and cervical cytology were performed before and after surgery, and residual or recurrent HSIL was assessed by colposcopy during follow-up. Generalized estimating equation (GEE) logistic regression accounted for within-patient clustering of genotype-specific HPV observations. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with HR-HPV persistence, and Firth's penalized logistic regression evaluated factors associated with residual or recurrent HSIL. Results Persistent HR-HPV infection rates were 23.3%, 19.0%, and 17.5% at 6, 12, and 18 months after LEEP, respectively. GEE analysis showed significant differences in type-specific persistence among the α 5/6, α 7, and α 9 species ( P = 0.024), with higher persistence in α 5/6 than α 7 (27.1% vs. 14.0%; OR = 2.30, 95% CI, 1.09–4.85; adjusted P = 0.024), but no significant differences between α 5/6 and α 9 or between α 7 and α 9. Multiple HR-HPV infections (OR = 2.76, 95% CI, 1.96–3.89; P < 0.001) and menopausal status (OR = 2.06, 95% CI, 1.18–3.66; P = 0.011), and positive endocervical margins (OR = 2.54, 95% CI, 1.48–4.32; P = 0.007) were associated with HR-HPV persistence. During follow-up, 32 patients (3.5%) developed residual or recurrent HSIL (21 residual, 11 recurrent). Firth's penalized regression identified persistent type-specific HR-HPV infection (OR = 21.88, 95% CI, 8.25–72.76; P < 0.001), number of involved cervical quadrants ( P = 0.025), endocervical involvement ( P = 0.006), and surgical margin status ( P < 0.001) as independently associated with residual or recurrent HSIL. Conclusions α 5/6 species showed a higher type-specific HR-HPV persistence than α 7 but not α 9 following LEEP. Multiple HR-HPV infections, menopausal status, and positive endocervical margins were associated with HR-HPV persistence. Persistent type-specific HR-HPV infection, multiple involved cervical quadrants, endocervical involvement, and positive surgical margins were independent predictors of residual or recurrent HSIL. Multicenter studies are warranted to validate integrating margin status with HPV genotyping for postoperative risk stratification.

title: Multifocal HPV-associated lesions of the anogenital region: clinical features, risk factors, pathogenesis, and prospects for a personalized approach. A review
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the leading etiological factor in the development of intraepithelial neoplasia’s and malignant neoplasms of the anogenital region. A distinctive clinical feature of the HPV-associated process is its propensity to form multifocal lesions, in which neoplasia’s of different anatomical sites – the cervix, vagina, vulva, and anal canal (CIN, VAIN, VIN, and AIN) – are detected either synchronously or metachronously during follow-up. Despite the high prevalence of this phenomenon, its pathogenetic basis remains a subject of debate. Existing interpretations predominantly regard such lesions as a set of independent local processes. In recent years, accumulating evidence has shown that HPV is capable of establishing persistent populations of infected cells that retain proliferative potential over extended periods. These changes create conditions for long-term viral persistence in epithelial tissues and maintenance of subclinical infection. In this context, multifocal HPV-associated lesions can be considered a manifestation of a single pathological process driven by prolonged viral persistence in the anogenital epithelium. Analysis of these mechanisms is of considerable interest for understanding the patterns of HPV infection spread, the development of multifocal neoplasia’s, and their clinical course. Multifocal HPV-associated lesions of the anogenital region reflect the complex, multilevel nature of the underlying pathogenesis and create significant challenges for their timely detection. In this setting, optimization of patient management requires a comprehensive diagnostic approach, including advanced visualization techniques, morphological and molecular-biological verification, as well as the development of personalized risk stratification strategies. These strategies aim to prevent disease progression and reduce the recurrence rate of precancerous lesions in the anogenital area.

title: Diagnostic potential of liquid biopsy in patients with HPV-associated diseases of the anogenital region. A review
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) represents the most prevalent sexually transmitted infection worldwide. According to data from the World Health Organization, over 290 million women globally are infected, with prevalence rates among sexually active individuals ranging from 50% to 80%. The high prevalence of oncogenic HPV significantly contributes to the development of cervical, vulvar, vaginal, and anal cancers. This underscores the clinical relevance of the infection and emphasizes the need to identify the earliest and most informative diagnostic methods. The minimally invasive liquid biopsy technique, which detects viral and tumor nucleic acids in biological fluids such as blood, urine, and saliva, offers new avenues for diagnosing and predicting precancerous and malignant diseases of the anogenital region. In contrast to traditional biopsy methods that require surgical intervention to obtain tissue samples, liquid biopsy is a safe, painless alternative that allows repeated testing at necessary intervals. To date, several biomarkers with promising diagnostic potential have been identified in gynecological oncology. Among these, microRNAs (miRNAs) – short non-coding RNAs that regulate post-transcription gene expression – have emerged as particularly noteworthy. In the context of HPV-associated carcinogenesis, the viral infection induces alterations in miRNA expression within infected epithelial cells, which subsequently leads to distinctive changes in their profiles in blood, urine, and saliva. These characteristics position miRNAs as potential candidates for the development of non-invasive diagnostic panels, warranting further investigation in this field.

title: Development of a machine learning model for risk stratification of cervical cancer based on cross-sectional data
abstract: Abstract Background Cervical cancer ranks as the fourth most common malignancy among women worldwide, with particularly poor prognosis and high rates of late-stage diagnosis in low- and middle-income countries. The current FIGO staging system has limited prognostic precision at the individual-level risk assessment, underscoring the need for diagnostic tools to support timely clinical decision-making. Methods This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning model that combines clinical, molecular, and cytological features for individualized risk stratification of cervical cancer at a single point in time. A total of 207 participants from the Fifth Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University were enrolled, including 151 non-cancer and 56 cancer cases. Over 20 variables were collected, including age, blood pressure, HPV genotypes, P16 expression, serum tumor markers (e.g., SCC, CEA, HE4), and cytological grading. Feature selection was performed using LASSO regression-based feature ranking, and the optimal number of predictors was determined by evaluating Random Forest (RF) performance across different feature subsets, resulting in 11 core predictors (e.g., SCC, HPV16/18, HSIL). Results Eleven machine learning models were evaluated. RF and LR demonstrated the strongest overall performance, with RF achieving the highest AUROC (0.966) and sensitivity (100%) among the evaluated models. RF was subsequently selected as the final model based on its balanced discrimination and calibration performance. SHAP analysis identified SCC, HPV16/18, and documented P16 status as major contributors. A nomogram was constructed for clinical visualization and interpretation. Conclusions This study presents an interpretable machine learning model for cross-sectional risk stratification of cervical cancer, providing a potential approach to support individualized screening and diagnostic decision-making. Further multicenter validation and integration of longitudinal data are warranted to enhance generalizability and future prognostic use. We acknowledge that the current findings are based on single-center data, and external validation is a key next step.

title: Advances in the application of gene methylation detection in cervical cancer screening
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a leading malignancy among women globally, with its pathogenesis strongly associated with persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. Despite the widespread adoption of HPV testing in cervical cancer screening, its suboptimal specificity frequently results in overdiagnosis and overtreatment. Gene methylation, a key epigenetic modification, has emerged as a highly specific biomarker associated with cervical precancerous lesions and carcinogenesis, holding significant promise for enhancing screening precision. This review comprehensively summarizes recent advances in gene methylation detection for cervical cancer screening, with a focus on the identification of methylation biomarkers, the evolution of detection technologies, and their clinical utility. Furthermore, it addresses the current challenges and limitations in implementing methylation-based assays in routine clinical practice. By offering a systematic overview of the field, this work aims to support the optimization of cervical cancer screening strategies and promote the integration of epigenetic biomarkers into standard clinical workflows.

title: Female pubic hair removal and adverse urogenital health outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Introduction Female pubic hair removal is a widespread practice shaped by aesthetic, cultural, and hygienic factors, with rising global prevalence, particularly in Western countries. Recent studies link extreme or frequent removal to adverse outcomes such as sexually transmitted infections, urinary tract infections, and vaginal microbiota alterations, yet the absence of evidence-based clinical guidelines limits consistent professional recommendations. Objective This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the scientific evidence on the urogenital effects of female pubic hair removal and aimed to develop evidence-based recommendations for safer clinical and hygienic practices. Methods A systematic search of Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, EBSCO, ScienceDirect, and ProQuest was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. Studies published between 2020 and 2025, in English or Spanish, addressing female pubic hair removal and its urogenital effects were included; fifteen studies met the inclusion criteria. Methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute tools, and pooled effect estimates were calculated using a random-effects (DerSimonian–Laird) model. The review was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251138298). Results Fifteen studies were included (11 analytical cross-sectional, 3 prospective cohort/longitudinal, and 1 qualitative) across diverse geographical regions. The pooled random-effects odds ratio was 2.15 (95% CI: 1.16–3.98), indicating a significant association between pubic hair removal and adverse outcomes, including sexually transmitted infections, urinary tract infections, vulvovaginal infections, and human papillomavirus. Heterogeneity was high (I2 = 94.7%), reflecting variability in exposure definitions, diagnostic methods, and study populations. Conclusions Frequent or complete pubic hair removal was associated with increased odds of urogenital complications and may disrupt vaginal microbiota balance. title: The double barrier: coronavirus disease 2019 and cervical cancer screening disparities among women with disabilities in South Korea: a nationwide cohort study
abstract: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic has posed unprecedented challenges to healthcare systems, potentially exacerbating pre-existing health disparities. Women with disabilities face structural barriers to healthcare that may be intensified during public health crises. This study aimed to evaluate pandemic-period changes in cervical cancer screening inequities among women with disabilities in South Korea. We analyzed Korean National Health Insurance Service Database data on cervical cancer screening participation among women aged ≥ 20 years, totaling more than 21 million person-years from 2017 to 2020. Multivariable logistic regression compared 2020 screening participation with the 2017–2019 average, adjusting for age, income, and region. Subgroup analyses were stratified by disability status, severity, and disability type. Overall screening participation declined in 2020 (OR = 0.828; 95% CI = 0.827–0.830). The reduction was greater among women with disabilities (OR, 0.758; 95% CI, 0.751–0.765) than among women without disabilities (OR, 0.832; 95% CI, 0.830–0.833), and a post hoc heterogeneity analysis comparing adjusted subgroup estimates supported this difference (ratio of adjusted ORs, 0.911; 95% CI, 0.903–0.920; p < 0.001). Reductions were sharpest for impairments affecting communication: facial (OR = 0.692), speech (OR = 0.713), and hearing (OR = 0.728). Conversely, participation increased among women aged 20–29 (OR = 1.142) but dropped sharply for those aged ≥ 40 (e.g., 40–49: OR = 0.744). During the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic, cervical cancer screening participation declined more among women with disabilities than among those without disabilities, particularly among women with communication-related impairments. These findings suggest that pandemic-period disruptions may have widened pre-existing screening disparities despite universal screening coverage. Equity-focused strategies, such as accessible screening environments and human papillomavirus self-sampling, may help improve resilience and equity in preventive care during public health emergencies.

title: Adolescent Immunization Rates in a Medicaid Managed Care Population During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Louisiana, 2019-2023.
abstract: To assess changes in adolescent immunization rates among enrollees in a Louisiana Medicaid managed care organization from 2019 through 2023 and examine sociodemographic differences. Using Louisiana's immunization information system and Healthcare Effectiveness Data and Information Set (HEDIS) specifications, we calculated human papillomavirus, meningococcal, tetanus-diphtheria-acellular pertussis, and combined-series immunization rates and compared demographic trends from 2020 to 2023. Combined-series rates decreased from 45.6% in 2020 to 38.0% in 2022, then partially recovered to 42.6% in 2023. Trends were broadly similar by race and sex. Rural adolescents had consistently lower rates and a larger decrease, from 38.4% to 28.8%, followed by recovery to 37.2%. Spanish-speaking families maintained substantially higher rates and experienced a smaller decrease, from 66.9% in 2020 to 61.9% in 2022. Adolescent immunization rates decreased during the COVID-19 pandemic and had not fully recovered by 2023, with persistent rural disparities. Public Health Implications. Recovery efforts should prioritize rural Medicaid populations and identify practices associated with sustained coverage among Spanish-speaking families. (Am J Public Health. Published online ahead of print September 24, 2026:e1-e8. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308717).

title: Clinicopathological role of microRNA‐205, microRNA‐223 and microRNA‐590 in vulvar cancer
abstract: Vulvar cancer is a rare malignancy whose development involves environmental, immunologic, genetic and viral factors, including high-risk HPV infection.MicroRNAs (miRNAs/miRs) regulate key oncogenic pathways and may serve as biomarkers in gynecological cancers.However, limited data are available on the role of miR-205, miR-223 and miR-590 in vulvar carcinoma.The present study thus assessed their expression and clinical relevance.A total of 38 women with vulvar carcinoma were included in the study.miRNA expression was quantified using reverse transcription-quantitative PCR from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded surgical specimens.Among the enrolled patients, 25 had both tumor tissue and matched non-malignant vulvar tissue available for analysis, enabling paired comparisons and fold-change calculations, whereas 13 patients contributed tumor tissue only due to insufficient RNA yield from the matched non-malignant specimen.Statistical analyses included paired t-tests and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis.Clinicopathological features were evaluated using International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) staging and histological grading.The results revealed that miR-205 expression was higher in patients with advanced disease, with a significant difference observed between FIGO I-III and FIGO IV tumors.miR-223 expression exhibited a tendency toward an association with poorer tumor differentiation, suggesting its potential as an unfavorable prognostic indicator.miR-590 expression was associated with tumor grade, with higher levels detected in well-differentiated lesions; additionally, the absence of miR-590 expression was linked to a lower likelihood of malignancy, supporting its diagnostic value.A reduced expression of miR-223 was independently associated with an improved overall survival (log-rank, P=0.013).No significant associations between miR-205 or miR-590 and overall survival were identified.On the whole, the present study demonstrated that miR-205, miR-223 and miR-590 expression patterns are associated with the tumor stage, grading and survival outcomes of patients with vulvar cancer.These miRNAs may thus serve as diagnostic or prognostic biomarkers, with miR-223 exhibiting the strongest prognostic significance and miR-590 demonstrating diagnostic specificity.Due to the rarity of vulvar cancer, larger multicenter studies and international datasets are required to validate these findings and to further elucidate the biological roles of miRNAs in this malignancy.

title: Cervical biopsy strategy during colposcopy: evidence from a retrospective study
abstract: To study the factors affecting the detection of cervical precancerous lesions and cervical carcinoma during colposcopy and to provide evidence for optimizing colposcopy biopsy strategies. This is a single-center retrospective study which included 1007 female patients who underwent colposcopy and cervical biopsy between June 2022 and November 2023. The pathological results of the biopsies served as the reference standard. Factors related to the detection rate of cervical precancerous lesions and cervical carcinoma were analysed. Subgroup analyses were performed according to the different cervical transformation zones to compare the efficiency of different biopsy methods. Abnormal cytology and high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection had high predictive values for cervical precancerous lesions and cervical carcinoma. The accuracy of colposcopy was affected by the type of cervical transformation zone. Various biopsy methods offered distinct advantages depending on the type of transformation zone involved. For the type I transformation zone, the detection rates of high-grade lesions were higher in the four-quadrant directed biopsy group (31.4% vs. 21.2%, P = 0.038) and the multipoint biopsy group (28.4% vs. 12.5%, P = 0.001) than in the corresponding control groups. For the type II transformation zone, the detection rate of high-grade lesions was greater when multipoint biopsy was performed at ≥ 3 sites (21.7% vs. For the type III transformation zone, neither four-quadrant directed biopsy, multipoint biopsy, nor endocervical curettage (ECC) significantly improved the detection rate of high-grade lesions. This study provides a basis for determining biopsy strategy during colposcopy. Biopsy is recommended for patients with both high-risk HPV infection and abnormal cytology. Four-quadrant directed biopsy or multipoint biopsy is suggested for type I transformation zones, whereas multipoint targeted biopsy is suggested for type II transformation zones. The observation and management of type III transformation zones by colposcopy remain challenging.

title: Association Between the Cervicovaginal Microbiota and Tumor Characteristics in Cervical Cancer
abstract: Introduction: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus is a necessary step in cervical carcinogenesis; however, the development of neoplasia is also determined by the state of the local microbial and immune microenvironment. Lactobacillus deficiency, anaerobic dysbiosis, and inter-kingdom biofilms can sustain inflammation, damage to the epithelial barrier, and persistence of viral infection. Objective: To study the cervicovaginal microbiota in cervical cancer and to determine its association with histological type and characteristics of the tumor process. Materials and Methods: The study had an analytical case-control design with cross-sectional and prospective-analytical components and included two research arms of 100 women each: a clinical screening cohort without verified invasive cervical cancer and a cohort of patients with morphologically confirmed invasive cancer. Cervicovaginal biocenosis was investigated by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction using the "Femoflor-16" panel. Genotyping of 14 types of high-risk human papillomavirus, cytological assessment, and histological verification were performed. Statistical analysis included the Mann–Whitney U test, chi-square or Fisher's exact test, univariate and multivariate logistic regression, interaction analysis, and clustering of microbiome profiles. Results: In the clinical screening cohort, high-risk human papillomavirus was detected in 72% of women, microbial community type IV in 20%, cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or higher in 27%, Candida fungi in 56%, Gardnerella vaginalis in 59%, and their co-colonization in 30%. title: Improving Cervical Cancer Screening Equity Through HPV Self-Sampling in Rural Health Clinics in the United States: A Scoping Review Protocol
abstract: The purpose of the scoping review is to map and synthesize existing literature on implementing human papillomavirus (HPV) self-sampling tests among rural health clinics in the United States. Specifically, the scoping review aims to identify and map evidence related to feasibility, accessibility, barriers, uptake, and implementation of HPV self-sampling in rural health clinics.

title: Republication de : Evaluating the interpretation of Neck CT/MRI scans by ChatGPT-4V for detecting primary oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma: An exploratory study
abstract: Objectives Early and accurate detection of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and the subset of oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is essential for the therapy and the prognosis of patients. Computer tomography (CT) is the primary imaging modality and is currently evaluated manually by radiologists and head and neck oncologists. Since image recognition in the form of artificial intelligence (AI) was introduced recently with the large language model (LLM) ChatGPT-4V, this exploratory study for the first time evaluates the application of image recognition by ChatGPT in interpreting neck CT and MRI scans for OPSCC detection, and corresponding images without any oropharyngeal lesion. Materials and methods The most likely diagnosis based on the CT images for 100 CT cases (50 OPSCC, 50 without lesion) and the available corresponding 62 MRI cases (31 OPSCC, 31 without an oropharyngeal lesion) by ChatGPT-4V was rated by two independent reviewers and the overall performance was evaluated in terms of accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. Results In this study, ChatGPT-4V reached a sensitivity of 72% and a specificity of 78% in identifying OPSCC from CT images. For MRI scans, sensitivity was 80.6% and specificity 83.9%. Human papillomavirus-positive and more advanced lesions were detected more reliably. Discussion In this exploratory study of CT and MRI neck scans of the oropharynx, ChatGPT-4V demonstrated a mediocre performance for detecting OPSCC. Continued research and advancements in AI are essential to improve the reliability and clinical utility of LLMs for the interpretation of neck scans.
journal: Annales françaises d Oto-rhino-laryngologie et de Pathologie Cervico-faciale

title: Economic Evaluation of HPV-based Cervical Cancer Screening in Tanzania: Trade-Offs Between Management Strategies Following Extended HPV Genotyping
abstract: Background: Cervical cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women in Tanzania. As Tanzania transitions from visual inspection with acetic acid to human papillomavirus (HPV)-based screening with extended genotyping, evidence is needed to guide genotype-based management. The ScreenFire assay classifies high-risk HPV genotypes into four risk groups, with HPV Channel 4 (HPV39/51/56/59/68) representing the lowest-risk group, for which optimal management remains uncertain. This study evaluated the trade-offs of existing and potential future management strategies for women with HPV Channel 4. Methods: A deterministic decision tree compared four management strategies: Immediate Treatment, automated visual evaluation (AVE) Triage with Return to Routine Screening, AVE Triage with One-Year Surveillance, and One-Year Surveillance. Do Nothing (no screening) and Return to Routine Screening (no further management following HPV Channel 4 identification) were included as comparators. Effectiveness parameters were informed by data from the National Expansion of HPV-based Cervical Cancer Screening in Tanzania (NECST) study and Human Papillomavirus Automated Visual Evaluation (PAVE) Consortium. Costs were estimated from a societal perspective using micro-costing conducted in Tanzania. The primary outcome was incremental cost per cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN3) treated. Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses (PSA) evaluated parameter uncertainty, while threshold and scenario analyses explored alternative implementation conditions. Results: Immediate Treatment achieved the greatest clinical benefit, treating most CIN3 lesions while leaving the fewest untreated. Despite the highest costs and greatest number of treatment procedures, it remained the only economically efficient strategy, with an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of 5,093,321 Tanzanian Shillings (TZS; US$2,033) per additional CIN3 treated. In PSA, Immediate Treatment became most likely to be optimal at a hypothetical willingness-to-pay value of approximately 5,400,000 TZS (US$2,155) per additional CIN3 treated. One-Year Surveillance was not economically efficient, while AVE-based triage remained near the efficiency frontier. Threshold and scenario analyses showed that AVE performance depended on diagnostic accuracy and implementation context, becoming economically efficient when Immediate Treatment was infeasible. Conclusion: These findings quantify trade-offs between clinical benefit, costs, and treatment burden across management strategies for HPV Channel 4 and may inform screening policies in Tanzania. Strategies may be adapted to treatment capacity, diagnostic performance, and feasibility.

title: Machine Learning-Driven Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (SERS) Profiling of Low Molecular Weight Serum from Cervical Cancer Patients
abstract: Cervical cancer is a leading contributor to both mortality and morbidity in low- and middle-income countries with Human papillomavirus (HPV) which is a small, nonenveloped virus containing a double-stranded circular DNA genome, identified as the predominant cause. The survival rate increases up to 95% when cervical cancer is detected through early-stage screening. In this work, surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS), an enhanced version of Raman spectroscopy, using silver nanoparticles (Ag-NPs) as a SERS substrate, has been explored for the rapid monitoring of biochemical variations identified among the various stages of cervical carcinoma patients as compared to healthy ones. Human blood is a rich source of biomolecules, in which high-molecular-weight fractions (HMWF) often mask low-molecular-weight fractions (LMWF), which contain disease-related biomarkers. Centrifugal filtration with a 100 kDa cutoff value is performed to separate HMWF from LMWF for SERS spectral identification and analysis of disease biomarkers. The SERS spectral features of 100 kDa filtrate fractions of disease samples are found at 353, 562, 766, 1180, 1307, 1365, 1508, and 1653 cm−1, as compared to peaks visible in healthy filtrate samples. Furthermore, the SERS spectra of various samples (cancerous and controlled) have been classified by principal component analysis (PCA) and partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA). Using validated PLS-DA analysis, the normal and cancerous samples are successfully identified and distinguished with 99% sensitivity and 95% specificity, and the K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) model is used to check similarity between samples which confirms the mean accuracy of 94.79%.

source_records.title: Machine Learning-Driven Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (SERS) Profiling of Low Molecular Weight Serum from Cervical Cancer Patients
source_records.abstract: Cervical cancer is a leading contributor to both mortality and morbidity in low- and middle-income countries with Human papillomavirus (HPV) which is a small, nonenveloped virus containing a double-stranded circular DNA genome, identified as the predominant cause. The survival rate increases up to 95% when cervical cancer is detected through early-stage screening. In this work, surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS), an enhanced version of Raman spectroscopy, using silver nanoparticles (Ag-NPs) as a SERS substrate, has been explored for the rapid monitoring of biochemical variations identified among the various stages of cervical carcinoma patients as compared to healthy ones. Human blood is a rich source of biomolecules, in which high-molecular-weight fractions (HMWF) often mask low-molecular-weight fractions (LMWF), which contain disease-related biomarkers. Centrifugal filtration with a 100 kDa cutoff value is performed to separate HMWF from LMWF for SERS spectral identification and analysis of disease biomarkers. The SERS spectral features of 100 kDa filtrate fractions of disease samples are found at 353, 562, 766, 1180, 1307, 1365, 1508, and 1653 cm−1, as compared to peaks visible in healthy filtrate samples. Furthermore, the SERS spectra of various samples (cancerous and controlled) have been classified by principal component analysis (PCA) and partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA). Using validated PLS-DA analysis, the normal and cancerous samples are successfully identified and distinguished with 99% sensitivity and 95% specificity, and the K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) model is used to check similarity between samples which confirms the mean accuracy of 94.79%.

title: Design, Synthesis and Biological Profiling of Fe(III)–Bipyridine Schiff Base Complexes: Experimental, Computational and Pharmacokinetic Insights
abstract: ABSTRACT Schiff base ligands and their transition metal complexes continue to attract attention for their versatile coordination behavior and biological relevance. Herein, three thiosemicarbazone ligands (L1–L3) were synthesized from para‐nitrobenzaldehyde and substituted thiosemicarbazides and converted to their corresponding iron(III)–bipyridine complexes (FT1–FT3). The compounds were characterized by FT–IR, UV–vis, 1 H/ 1 3 C NMR, ESI–MS, EPR, molar conductivity, and elemental analysis. Spectroscopic data confirmed coordination through the azomethine nitrogen and thione sulfur, evidenced by shifts in characteristic bands and new Fe─N and Fe─S vibrations. DFT optimization revealed a distorted octahedral geometry and provided HOMO–LUMO gaps, global reactivity descriptors, and molecular electrostatic potential maps. Anticancer (SiHa), antimycobacterial, and antifungal assays showed that FT3 was the most active, giving 72.85% antifungal inhibition at 1000 ppm together with improved anticancer and antibacterial activity. Molecular docking against HPV‐18 E2 (PDB 1F9F) and CYP51 (PDB 1EA1) gave favorable binding energies that correlated with the experimental trends, FT3 forming the most stable interactions. ADME predictions indicated broadly acceptable, though preliminary, pharmacokinetic behavior. Overall, these iron(III) Schiff base complexes display promising multi‐target activity warranting further mechanistic and preclinical study.

title: External genital HPV DNA positivity and type concordance among male partners of cervical HPV-positive women: a paired cross-sectional study
abstract: Data onexternal genital human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in male partners of cervical HPV-positive women are limited in Southwest China. We conducted a single-center study of 303 heterosexual couples in Kunming, China, from January 2024 to December 2025, with a 1:1 age-matched comparison of men with versus without external genital HPV DNA detected at baseline. Women had a newly positive cervical HPV DNA test, and male partners underwent standardized external genital HPV genotyping. Concordance was assessed in all 303 couples, and factors associated with prevalent male HPV DNA positivity were examined in 149 matched case-control pairs using conditional logistic regression with prespecified behavioral/anatomic variables; female multiple-type infection and HPV16/18 positivity were evaluated only in exploratory secondary analyses. Of 303 enrolled couples, 149 men (49.2%) had external genital HPV DNA detected at baseline, including 121 (39.9%) with at least one assay-designated high-risk genotype. Any shared genotype was present in 94/303 couples (31.0%; 95% CI, 26.1–36.4) and in 94/149 male HPV-positive couples (63.1%; 95% CI, 55.1–70.4), mainly involving HPV52, HPV16, and HPV58. In the primary matched model, inconsistent condom use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.17; 95% CI, 1.35–3.47; P = 0.001), current smoking (aOR, 1.61; 95% CI, 1.02–2.54; P = 0.041), being uncircumcised (aOR, 1.82; 95% CI, 1.01–3.23; P = 0.046), and four or more lifetime female partners (aOR, 1.82; 95% CI, 1.03–3.22; P = 0.039) were associated with higher odds of male HPV positivity. In a secondary analysis, female multiple-type infection was associated with male HPV positivity (aOR, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.00-2.63; P = 0.049). External genital HPV DNA positivity was common among male partners of cervical HPV-positive women, and 63.1% of male HPV-positive couples shared at least one genotype, most often HPV52, HPV16, or HPV58. These cross-sectional findings do not establish causation or transmission direction but support partner-aware counseling about vaccination eligibility, consistent condom use, and smoking cessation.

full_text: Abstract Background Vaccination against human papillomavirus (HPV) is an effective strategy for preventing cervical cancer. Morocco introduced the HPV vaccine into its National Immunization Program in 2022; however, vaccination coverage remains suboptimal. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of HPV vaccine refusal among adolescent girls and to identify the factors associated with refusal. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study in Morocco among middle school girls aged 11 to 14 years. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire administered through individual face-to-face interviews. The questionnaire assessed sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge of HPV and its vaccine, perceptions and beliefs regarding HPV vaccination, trust in the healthcare system, social influences, and perceived susceptibility to HPV infection. Results A total of 1,099 adolescent girls participated in the study, with a mean age of 13.0 ± 0.8 years. The prevalence of HPV vaccine refusal was 31.6%. After multivariable adjustment, HPV vaccine refusal was independently associated with the belief that the vaccine could cause infertility, a monthly household income above USD 999, previous parental refusal of at least one routine vaccine, paternal illiteracy, limited knowledge of the vaccine target population, poor awareness of cervical cancer and its prevention, concerns about vaccine side effects, low perceived susceptibility to HPV infection, and negative societal norms. Conversely, a monthly household income between USD 150 and USD 199, fear of regretting not receiving the HPV vaccine, and limited knowledge of cervical cancer complications were associated with a lower likelihood of HPV vaccine refusal. Conclusion HPV vaccine refusal among Moroccan adolescent girls was associated with inadequate knowledge, misconceptions about vaccine safety, low perceived susceptibility to HPV infection, socioeconomic characteristics, and sociocultural influences. These findings highlight the need for culturally tailored interventions that improve HPV-related knowledge, address misconceptions, and strengthen risk perception to increase HPV vaccine uptake in Morocco. All collected data were kept strictly confidential and were anonymized before analysis. Volume 32, Number 10—October 2026 Research Letter Human Papillomavirus Condylomas of Extragenital Site in Immunocompetent Man, New York, USA, 2025 Suggested citation for this article Abstract Human papillomavirus types 6 and 11 are associated with mucosal condylomata acuminata, with rare reports of extragenital manifestations. We report a case of condyloma localized to the neck of an immunocompetent heterosexual man, without concurrent anogenital lesions. Our findings challenge theories of the site-specific tropism of these human papillomavirus types. Human papillomavirus (HPV) types 6 and 11 have long been associated with condylomata acuminata, accounting for 90% of warts affecting the anogenital region (1). History of immunosuppression, both primary or secondary, is associated with HPV-related diseases, making affected patients susceptible to development of cutaneous and mucosal warts (2). Reports of extragenital manifestations of condylomas are rare, with previous cases being associated with pediatric populations, men who have sex with men, and persons with a history of HIV. We report a case of HPV types 6 and 11–positive condylomas localized to the lateral neck of an immunocompetent heterosexual man without concurrent anogenital involvement. In 2025, a heterosexual man in his 40s with an unremarkable medical history sought treatment for a growth on the right side of his neck present for 1 year prior, with reported increase in size. On examination, we noted 6 clustered verrucous-to-mamillated brown papules distributed along the right lateral neck (Figure). Our initial differential diagnosis included inflamed seborrheic keratoses and verruca vulgaris. We treated the lesions with cryotherapy, which provided temporary resolution. The patient returned to our clinic 11 months later for recurrence. We performed a shave biopsy, which showed papillated epidermal hyperplasia with hypergranulosis, compact orthokeratosis, and dilated blood vessels in the papillary dermis. HPV testing by in situ hybridization was positive for HPV types 6 and 11. Screening tests for sexually transmitted infections revealed negative results for gonorrhea, chlamydia, syphilis, and HIV. Complete blood count testing and a comprehensive metabolic panel also yielded results that were within reference limits. Immunologic screening revealed a positive antinuclear antibody titer of 1:80 (reference <1:40) but unremarkable levels of IgA, IgG, and IgM. Our case report challenges the traditional paradigm of HPV types 6 and 11 tropism to mucosal skin (3). Although reports do exist describing condylomas at extragenital cutaneous sites, those reports have largely involved children, patients with immunosuppression, or persons with concurrent genital involvement (4–6). One report described a patient with extragenital cutaneous HPV type 6 without genital involvement; however, the patient had a history of HIV (6). Although reports of extragenital condylomas and cutaneous HPV types 6 infection exist, cases of HPV types 6 and 11–positive extragenital cutaneous lesions in immunocompetent adults without concurrent anogenital disease are rare. HPV is known to affect mucosal tissue, particularly of the head and neck, with HPV types 16 accounting for most oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinomas (7). Of interest, HPV types 6 and 11 can be co-transmitted with higher-risk types of HPV in genital skin (8,9). Hypotheses for transmission to this area of the neck include autoinoculation, fomites, skin-to-skin contact with mucosal skin, or even vertical transmission (10). A limitation in our case report was the inability to distinguish between HPV types 6 and 11 based on laboratory in situ hybridization technique. Nonetheless, this case highlights the possibility of condylomas in nonanogenital cutaneous sites in immunocompetent hosts, emphasizing that practitioners should consider biopsy with HPV typing in atypical verrucous lesions on cutaneous sites. Ms. Fong is a research fellow at New York University Grossman School of Medicine. Her research interests include dermatology, infectious diseases, and artificial intelligence applications in medicine. Dr. Zampella is an associate professor of dermatology at New York University Grossman School of Medicine and a board-certified dermatologist at New York University Langone’s Preston Robert Tisch Center for Men’s Health. His clinical and academic interests include medical, surgical, and cosmetic dermatology, with particular focus on men’s health, LGBTQ+ dermatology, and complex inflammatory skin disease. full_text: Abstract Accurate human papillomavirus (HPV) genotype classification from genomic sequences remains challenging because of the high sequence similarity among closely related HPV types. Although deep learning has been increasingly applied to viral sequence analysis, most existing studies rely on limited genomic regions, handcrafted features, or evaluate individual models under different datasets and experimental settings, making direct performance comparisons difficult. To address this limitation, we establish a unified experimental framework that enables a fair comparison of representative deep learning architectures under shared preprocessing, encoding, and data-partitioning procedures and a standardized training protocol. We formulate HPV genotype classification as an eight-class prediction task using fixed-length 5,000-bp genome sequence windows, including six high-risk genotypes (HPV16, HPV18, HPV31, HPV35, HPV52, and HPV58) and two low-risk genotypes (HPV11 and HPV42). Within this unified framework, we evaluate five widely used deep learning architectures: CNN, Conv-BiLSTM, Conv-BiGRU, a patch-based Transformer Encoder, and TCN. All models are trained and evaluated using the same quality-controlled dataset, ambiguity-aware four-channel nucleotide encoding, leakage-free stratified data partitioning, and a unified optimization protocol. The results show that CNN achieves the best overall performance, reaching 99.36% accuracy with a macro F1-score of 0.99. Despite its simpler architecture and lower parameter count, CNN outperforms the recurrent, attention-based, and temporal convolutional alternatives in the held-out test evaluation. These findings demonstrate that carefully controlled experimental settings are as important as model complexity for the fair evaluation of deep learning models in genomic sequence classification. The proposed framework provides a controlled basis for future studies on HPV genotype classification and for the comparative evaluation of deep learning models.
